captions: This is the Moneyview I P O, a mainboard offer,
open from the twenty-fourth to the twenty-eighth of September,
closing today.
The price band is ₹32 to ₹34.
Every figure here comes from the final red herring prospectus
and exchange notices;
the final price is fixed after bidding,
so valuations are computed at the ₹34 cap.
First, the business.
Moneyview is a digital lending platform.
Its app had 134.14 million registered users by March 2026.
Most personal loans are funded by 48 financial partners,
with its own NBFC, Whizdm Finance, also lending.
The managed book of unsecured personal loans was ₹21,380.14 Cr,
and annualised losses on those loans eased to 6.95% in FY26.
The financial checkpoint.
FY26 revenue was ₹3,351.16 Cr, against ₹2,339.15 Cr in FY25,
a change of 43.26%.
Profit after tax was ₹242.71 Cr, a margin of 7.24%.
One detail matters here.
Reported profit includes a ₹206.65 Cr exceptional charge,
mostly a one-time ₹160 Cr performance incentive to the MD and CEO.
Before exceptional items, FY26 profit was ₹397.34 Cr.
Also note loan impairments of ₹983.53 Cr in FY26,
the core risk in unsecured lending.
The offer size at the cap is ₹1,091.68 Cr.
₹750.00 Cr is fresh issue that goes into the company,
and ₹341.68 Cr is an offer for sale that goes to selling shareholders.
So 68.70% of the deal is new capital,
and 31.30% is an exit for existing holders.
Where does the money go?
Of the ₹750.00 Cr fresh issue,
₹325.00 Cr funds default-loss-guarantee arrangements,
the deposits that let lending partners disburse more loans through Moneyview.
₹250.00 Cr strengthens the capital of its NBFC, Whizdm Finance.
The offer for sale is about ₹341.68 Cr at the cap,
sold by investors including Accel, Internet Fund III and Ribbit,
and by the founders.
Valuation.
At the ₹34 cap,
the price is 21.66x reported FY26 diluted earnings of ₹1.57 a share.
Listed peers range from OnEMI at 16.62x,
SBI Cards 27.98x and Bajaj Finance 33.66x,
to PB Fintech at 120.33x.
Remember the reported figure already carries the one-time charge;
on pre-exceptional profit the multiple would be lower.
Now balance the evidence.
Watch-out:
Unsecured loans:
₹983.53 Cr impairment in FY26.
Strength:
Revenue up 43.26% to ₹3,351.16 Cr.
Watch-out:
Default-loss guarantees keep credit risk on its books.
Strength:
Profit before exceptional items up 65.37%.
Watch-out:
31.30% of the offer is investor OFS.
Strength:
21.66x P/E, below Bajaj Finance and SBI Cards.
How to apply.
The minimum bid is one lot of 441 shares,
which is ₹14,994 at the cap.
Retail investors can bid up to two lakh rupees,
and allotment is by lottery if retail is oversubscribed.
Check live subscription on the N S E or B S E website,
not social media.
Let's recap.
FY26 revenue ₹3,351.16 Cr, profit ₹242.71 Cr.
The offer is ₹1,091.68 Cr,
of which ₹341.68 Cr is offer for sale.
Valuation is 21.66x earnings at the cap.
The minimum investment is ₹14,994.
This video is public-source education from the red herring
prospectus and exchange notices.
It is not investment advice and not a buy or sell call.
Read the final documents,
check live subscription on the exchange,
and consult a SEBI-registered adviser.
Thanks for watching.
